# Pathway Enrichment and Multi-Omics Abundance Profiles

Pathway enrichment and multi-omics profiling aggregate molecular alterations into functional signatures. This chapter covers Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), multi-omics pathway enrichment across RNA, single-cell transcriptomics, mass spectrometry proteomics, and microbiome metagenomics, bubble heatmap archetypes, and rank-abundance dynamic range curves.

## Gene Set Enrichment Analysis: `type = "gsea"` and `type = "gsea_running"`

Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (Subramanian et al., *PNAS* 2005) evaluates whether an a priori defined gene set $S$ shows cumulative enrichment at the extremes of a ranked gene list $L$:

$$P_{\text{hit}}(S, i) = \sum_{g_j \in S, j \le i} \frac{|r_j|^p}{N_R}, \quad N_R = \sum_{g_j \in S} |r_j|^p$$

$$P_{\text{miss}}(S, i) = \sum_{g_j \notin S, j \le i} \frac{1}{N - N_H}$$

$$ES(S) = \arg\max_{i} |P_{\text{hit}}(S, i) - P_{\text{miss}}(S, i)|$$

`cliomicplot` provides four complementary visualizations for GSEA results:
1. **Preranked Enrichment Dot Plot (`type = "gsea"`)**: Pathway terms ranked by effect magnitude, with dot size encoding $-\log_{10}(\text{FDR})$ and fill encoding Normalized Enrichment Score (NES).
2. **Three-Tier Running Score Walk Plot (`type = "gsea_running"`)**: The classical GSEA profile displaying the cumulative walk curve, gene hit barcode rug, and ranked metric area.
3. **Directional Diverging Lollipop Plot (`type = "lollipop"`)**: Horizontal effect size bars comparing positive and negative pathway activation.
4. **Multi-Phenotype Comparison Matrix (`type = type_bubble_diverging()`)**: Cross-condition pathway activity across disease phenotypes and therapeutic stages.

### Example 1: Preranked Pathway Enrichment Dot Plot

The dot plot displays top enriched pathways sorted by absolute NES, highlighting concurrent upregulation of inflammatory signaling and downregulation of lipid metabolism:

```{r gsea-dotplot-demo, fig.width=8.0, fig.height=5.5}
library(cliomicplot)
library(ggplot2)

pathways <- c(
  "Cytokine-Cytokine Receptor Interaction", "JAK-STAT Signaling Pathway",
  "Toll-like Receptor Signaling", "Th1 and Th2 Cell Differentiation",
  "Chemokine Signaling Pathway", "NF-kappa B Signaling",
  "IL-17 Signaling Pathway", "Antigen Processing and Presentation",
  "T Cell Receptor Signaling", "B Cell Receptor Signaling",
  "Natural Killer Cell Mediated Cytotoxicity", "Apoptosis",
  "Fatty Acid Metabolism", "Steroid Biosynthesis", "Keratinization"
)

gsea_df <- data.frame(
  Term = pathways,
  NES  = c(2.65, 2.38, 2.15, 2.08, 1.95, 1.88, 1.72, 1.65, 1.45, 1.25, 0.95, 0.82, -1.65, -1.98, -2.45),
  FDR  = c(1e-5, 2e-5, 8e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4, 5e-4, 1e-3, 2e-3, 5e-3, 0.015, 0.045, 0.082, 0.002, 0.0005, 0.0001)
)

clitheme("nature")

p_gsea <- cliplot(
  gsea_df,
  type     = "gsea",
  top_term = 15,
  title    = "Normalized Enrichment Scores Across Inflammatory Cascades"
)
p_gsea
```

### Example 2: Three-Tier GSEA Running Enrichment Score Walk

The running enrichment score walk illustrates the cumulative enrichment score $ES(i)$ across ranked genes, identifying the leading-edge subset that accounts for peak enrichment:

```{r gsea-running-demo, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=6.2}
set.seed(42)

# Simulate transcriptome ranking of 1,200 genes sorted by differential expression t-statistic
all_genes <- paste0("Gene_", seq_len(1200))
stats <- sort(rnorm(1200, mean = 0, sd = 2.0), decreasing = TRUE)
names(stats) <- all_genes

# Define target gene set (40 genes enriched at the top of the ranked list)
pathway_hits <- all_genes[c(seq(2, 80, by = 2), seq(90, 300, by = 20))]

# Compute exact running enrichment walk using Subramanian algorithm
walk_df <- cli_calc_gsea_running(stats, pathway_hits, p = 1.0)

# Render 3-tier composite: Running ES curve, Barcode rug, and Ranked metric gradient
p_running <- cliplot(
  walk_df,
  type = type_gsea_running(
    line_col     = "#1B7837",
    line_width   = 1.1,
    barcode_col  = "#182033",
    show_metric  = TRUE,
    peak_color   = "#D73027",
    pathway_name = "Hallmark IL-4 / IL-13 Signaling Pathway",
    nes          = 2.45,
    fdr          = 0.0001
  )
)
p_running
```

### Example 3: Directional Diverging Lollipop Enrichment Plot

Horizontal lollipops provide a clean visualization of pathway activation versus repression relative to the zero null baseline:

```{r gsea-lollipop-demo, fig.width=8.0, fig.height=4.8}
pathway_subset <- c(
  "Cytokine-Cytokine Receptor", "JAK-STAT Cascade", "Th2 Differentiation",
  "Chemokine Cascade", "NF-kB Activation", "IL-17 Signaling",
  "Fatty Acid Metabolism", "Keratinization", "Steroid Biosynthesis"
)
nes_subset <- c(2.65, 2.38, 2.08, 1.95, 1.88, 1.72, -1.65, -1.98, -2.45)

lollipop_df <- data.frame(
  Term = pathway_subset,
  NES  = nes_subset,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
lollipop_df$Term <- factor(lollipop_df$Term, levels = lollipop_df$Term[order(lollipop_df$NES)])

clitheme("science")

p_lollipop <- cliplot(
  NES ~ Term,
  data = lollipop_df,
  type = type_lollipop(
    point_size  = 3.8,
    stem_width  = 0.8,
    point_color = "#3B4992"
  ),
  title = "Directional Pathway Enrichment Relative to Zero Baseline",
  xlab  = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)"
) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4)
p_lollipop
```

### Example 4: Multi-Phenotype GSEA Comparison Matrix

Comparing pathway enrichment across multiple experimental contrasts reveals shared inflammatory mechanisms and disease-specific divergences:

```{r gsea-comparison-matrix-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.8}
set.seed(101)
pheno_pathways <- c(
  "IL-4 / IL-13 Signaling", "Th2 Differentiation", "JAK-STAT Cascade",
  "Chemokine Receptor Activity", "Epidermal Differentiation", "Lipid Synthesis"
)
comparisons <- c("AD LS vs Healthy", "AD NL vs Healthy", "AD LS vs NL", "Dupilumab W16")

multi_gsea <- expand.grid(Pathway = pheno_pathways, Comparison = comparisons, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
multi_gsea$NES <- c(
  2.6, 0.8, 2.1, -1.8,
  2.3, 0.5, 1.9, -1.6,
  1.9, 0.6, 1.5, -1.2,
  2.0, 0.4, 1.7, -1.1,
  -2.4, -0.6, -2.1, 1.8,
  -2.1, -0.4, -1.8, 1.5
)
multi_gsea$FDR <- c(
  1e-4, 0.08, 2e-4, 5e-4,
  3e-4, 0.12, 4e-4, 8e-4,
  2e-3, 0.10, 5e-3, 0.01,
  1e-3, 0.15, 3e-3, 0.02,
  2e-4, 0.09, 3e-4, 1e-3,
  5e-4, 0.14, 8e-4, 2e-3
)

clitheme("nature")

p_multi_gsea <- cliplot(
  Pathway ~ Comparison,
  data       = multi_gsea,
  by         = -log10(multi_gsea$FDR),
  type       = type_bubble_diverging(
    palette      = "nature",
    midpoint     = 0,
    max_size     = 7.5,
    stroke_col   = "grey30",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)),
    fill_name    = "NES"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = multi_gsea$NES),
  title      = "Cross-Phenotype Pathway Enrichment Concordance",
  subtitle   = "Circle size encodes -log10 q; fill encodes Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)"
)
p_multi_gsea
```

## Multi-Omics Pathway Enrichment: RNA, Single-Cell, Proteomics, and Microbiome

Enrichment analysis connects high-dimensional molecular measurements to cellular mechanisms across four biological layers:
- **Bulk RNA-seq**: Hypergeometric over-representation of differentially expressed genes against background universes.
- **Single-cell RNA-seq**: Cell-level module signature scores tested for lineage specificity by Wilcoxon rank-sum tests.
- **Mass Spectrometry Proteomics**: Moderated $t$-tests followed by protein complex Fisher exact test fold enrichment.
- **Microbial Metagenomics**: Quality-filtered MetaCyc pathway abundance tests across anatomical sites.

### Bulk RNA-seq Over-Representation Analysis (ORA): A to Z Pipeline

In bulk transcriptomics, Over-Representation Analysis tests whether pathway genes appear in the differentially expressed gene set more frequently than expected under the hypergeometric distribution:

$$P(X \ge k) = \sum_{i=k}^{\min(|S|, |D|)} \frac{\binom{|S|}{i} \binom{N - |S|}{|D| - i}}{\binom{N}{|D|}}$$

where $N$ is total measured background genes, $|D|$ is significant DEGs, $|S|$ is pathway size in the universe, and $k$ is observed overlap.

The pipeline starts from DESeq2 differential results in `geo_dermatology_series_de.rds`, identifies upregulated DEGs ($p_{\text{adj}} < 0.01$, $\log_2(\text{FC}) > 1.2$), tests pathway gene sets with `cli_calc_ora()`, and plots Gene Ratio $\frac{k}{|D|}$ with FDR tiers:

```{r multiomics-rna-ora-atoz, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.6}
# Step 1: Load differential expression results from GEO series
series <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "geo_dermatology_series_de.rds", package = "cliomicplot"))
de_tbl <- series[["ad_vs_hc"]]

# Step 2: Define DEG criteria and extract measured background universe
de_genes <- de_tbl$gene[which(de_tbl$padj < 0.01 & de_tbl$log2FC > 1.2)]
bg_genes <- de_tbl$gene

# Step 3: Define curated cutaneous pathway gene sets
skin_pathways <- list(
  "IL-4 / IL-13 Signaling"        = c("IL4R", "IL13RA1", "STAT6", "CCL17", "CCL18", "CCL22", "CCL26", "SOCS1", "POSTN"),
  "Epidermal Differentiation"     = c("FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3A", "LCE3D", "LCE3E", "SPRR2G", "SPRR1A", "KRT10"),
  "Antimicrobial Defense"         = c("DEFB4A", "S100A7", "S100A8", "S100A9", "S100A12", "PI3", "CAMP", "LTF"),
  "Alarmins & Epithelial Stress"  = c("IL33", "TSLP", "IL1RL1", "S100A8", "S100A9", "HMGB1"),
  "Serine Peptidase Inhibitors"   = c("SERPINB3", "SERPINB4", "SPINK5", "SERPINA1", "SERPINA3"),
  "Fatty Acid & Lipid Metabolism" = c("FASN", "ELOVL3", "ELOVL4", "ELOVL6", "SCD", "ACACA", "FABP5")
)

# Step 4: Run statistical over-representation analysis (Hypergeometric test + BH FDR)
ora_res <- cli_calc_ora(de_genes, skin_pathways, background = bg_genes)
ora_res$Pathway <- factor(ora_res$Pathway, levels = ora_res$Pathway[order(ora_res$GeneRatio)])

# Step 5: Visualize pathway coverage and significance
clitheme("nature")

p_rna_ora <- ggplot2::ggplot(ora_res, ggplot2::aes(x = GeneRatio, y = Pathway)) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    ggplot2::aes(x = 0, xend = GeneRatio, y = Pathway, yend = Pathway),
    color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(size = Count, fill = -log10(padj)),
    shape = 21, color = "grey25", stroke = 0.45
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("#EFF3FF", "#6BAED6", "#2171B5", "#08519C"),
    name = expression(-log[10]~italic(q))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_area(max_size = 7.5, name = "DEG Count") +
  theme_cli_nature() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Gene Ratio (k / |D|)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Bulk Transcriptomic Over-Representation Analysis (Lesional vs Healthy)",
    subtitle = "Gene ratio denotes pathway representation; point size reflects significant DEG count"
  )
p_rna_ora
```

Antimicrobial defense had the strongest enrichment ($q = 1.06 \times 10^{-11}$, fold enrichment 47.4), followed by epidermal differentiation ($q = 6.52 \times 10^{-7}$) and IL-4 / IL-13 signaling ($q = 9.61 \times 10^{-7}$).

### Single-Cell scRNA-seq Lineage Pathway Signatures: A to Z Pipeline

Single-cell pathway scoring computes cell-level activity for gene signatures, then evaluates lineage-specific activation by non-parametric testing:

1. Standardize expression values across cells ($z$-score).
2. Calculate cell-wise signature module scores as mean expression across signature genes.
3. Quantify active cells ($\text{Score} > 0$) per lineage.
4. Test lineage specificity using two-sample Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.

```{r multiomics-scrna-pathway-atoz, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.8}
# Step 1: Construct single-cell expression matrix across 7 lineages
set.seed(42)
cell_types <- c("Basal KC", "Spinous KC", "Suprabasal KC", "CD4+ Th2", "ILC2", "cDC2", "Fibroblasts")
n_per_type <- 60
cells <- rep(cell_types, each = n_per_type)
n_cells <- length(cells)

all_sc_genes <- c(
  "IL4R", "IL13RA1", "STAT6", "CCL17", "CCL22",
  "IL33", "TSLP", "IL1RL1", "S100A8", "S100A9",
  "FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3A", "SPRR2G",
  "HLA-DRA", "HLA-DRB1", "CD74", "CD86",
  "COL1A1", "COL1A2", "FN1", "MMP1",
  paste0("ControlGene_", 1:25)
)

sc_mat <- matrix(rnorm(n_cells * length(all_sc_genes), mean = 0.5, sd = 0.8),
                 nrow = length(all_sc_genes), ncol = n_cells,
                 dimnames = list(all_sc_genes, paste0("Cell_", seq_len(n_cells))))
sc_mat[sc_mat < 0] <- 0

# Set lineage-specific expression programs
sc_mat[c("IL4R", "IL13RA1", "CCL17", "CCL22"), cells %in% c("CD4+ Th2", "ILC2")] <-
  sc_mat[c("IL4R", "IL13RA1", "CCL17", "CCL22"), cells %in% c("CD4+ Th2", "ILC2")] + 2.8
sc_mat[c("FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3A", "SPRR2G"), cells %in% c("Spinous KC", "Suprabasal KC")] <-
  sc_mat[c("FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3A", "SPRR2G"), cells %in% c("Spinous KC", "Suprabasal KC")] + 3.2
sc_mat[c("HLA-DRA", "HLA-DRB1", "CD74", "CD86"), cells == "cDC2"] <-
  sc_mat[c("HLA-DRA", "HLA-DRB1", "CD74", "CD86"), cells == "cDC2"] + 3.5
sc_mat[c("COL1A1", "COL1A2", "FN1", "MMP1"), cells == "Fibroblasts"] <-
  sc_mat[c("COL1A1", "COL1A2", "FN1", "MMP1"), cells == "Fibroblasts"] + 3.0

sc_signatures <- list(
  "Type 2 Cytokines"          = c("IL4R", "IL13RA1", "STAT6", "CCL17", "CCL22"),
  "Alarmin Cascade"           = c("IL33", "TSLP", "IL1RL1", "S100A8", "S100A9"),
  "Epidermal Differentiation" = c("FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3A", "SPRR2G"),
  "Antigen Presentation"      = c("HLA-DRA", "HLA-DRB1", "CD74", "CD86"),
  "Extracellular Matrix"      = c("COL1A1", "COL1A2", "FN1", "MMP1")
)

# Step 2: Calculate per-cell module signature scores
scale_mat <- t(scale(t(sc_mat)))
module_scores <- vapply(sc_signatures, function(sig_genes) {
  colMeans(scale_mat[intersect(sig_genes, rownames(scale_mat)), , drop = FALSE])
}, numeric(n_cells))

# Step 3: Compute lineage summary metrics and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests
sc_res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sc_signatures), function(sig_name) {
  scores <- module_scores[, sig_name]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(cell_types), function(ct) {
    in_ct <- cells == ct
    pct_active <- mean(scores[in_ct] > 0) * 100
    mean_val   <- mean(scores[in_ct])
    wt <- wilcox.test(scores[in_ct], scores[!in_ct], alternative = "greater")
    data.frame(
      Pathway    = sig_name,
      CellType   = ct,
      PctActive  = pct_active,
      MeanScore  = mean_val,
      pvalue     = wt$p.value,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))
sc_res$padj <- p.adjust(sc_res$pvalue, method = "BH")

# Step 4: Render publication circle bubble heatmap
clitheme("cell")

p_sc_path <- cliplot(
  Pathway ~ CellType,
  data = sc_res,
  by   = sc_res$PctActive,
  type = type_bubble_circle(
    palette      = "plasma",
    max_size     = 7.5,
    stroke_col   = "grey35",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = "% Active Cells",
    fill_name    = "Mean Score"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = sc_res$MeanScore),
  title      = "Cell-Type-Resolved Pathway Activation in Inflammatory Skin",
  subtitle   = "Point size reflects percentage of active cells; colour reflects mean module score"
)
p_sc_path
```

Type 2 cytokine cascade localized to CD4+ Th2 and ILC2 cells (100% active, mean scores 1.13 and 1.11, $q < 10^{-23}$), whereas epidermal differentiation restricted to spinous and suprabasal keratinocytes ($q < 10^{-20}$).

### Mass Spectrometry Proteomics Functional Module Enrichment: A to Z Pipeline

Skin mass spectrometry proteomics measures translated protein quantities. The analysis pipeline:

1. Tests protein differential abundance between clinical groups with two-sample $t$-tests ($q < 0.01$, $|\log_2\text{FC}| > 1.0$).
2. Maps significant proteins to functional macromolecular complexes.
3. Tests module over-representation by Fisher's exact test.
4. Computes mean complex $\log_2(\text{FC})$ to capture directional protein remodeling.

```{r multiomics-proteomics-modules-atoz, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.8}
# Step 1: Input LFQ protein intensity matrix across 6 biological replicates
set.seed(42)
proteins <- c(
  "FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3D", "SPRR2A",
  "DSC1", "DSG1", "DSP", "PKP1",
  "SPINK5", "SERPINB3", "SERPINB4",
  "S100A7", "S100A8", "S100A9", "DEFB4A",
  "ATP5F1A", "NDUFS1", "COX4I1", "SDHA",
  paste0("Protein_Background_", 1:150)
)
n_reps <- 6

lfq_hc <- matrix(rnorm(length(proteins) * n_reps, mean = 24, sd = 0.5), nrow = length(proteins))
lfq_ad <- matrix(rnorm(length(proteins) * n_reps, mean = 24, sd = 0.5), nrow = length(proteins))
rownames(lfq_hc) <- rownames(lfq_ad) <- proteins

# AD-specific protein shifts
lfq_ad[c("FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3D", "SPRR2A"), ] <- lfq_ad[c("FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3D", "SPRR2A"), ] - 2.5
lfq_ad[c("DSC1", "DSG1", "DSP", "PKP1"), ] <- lfq_ad[c("DSC1", "DSG1", "DSP", "PKP1"), ] - 1.8
lfq_ad[c("SPINK5", "SERPINB3", "SERPINB4"), ] <- lfq_ad[c("SPINK5", "SERPINB3", "SERPINB4"), ] + 2.4
lfq_ad[c("S100A7", "S100A8", "S100A9", "DEFB4A"), ] <- lfq_ad[c("S100A7", "S100A8", "S100A9", "DEFB4A"), ] + 3.2

# Step 2: Moderated statistical testing for differentially abundant proteins
de_prot <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(proteins), function(i) {
  tt <- t.test(lfq_ad[i, ], lfq_hc[i, ])
  data.frame(
    Protein = proteins[i],
    log2FC  = mean(lfq_ad[i, ]) - mean(lfq_hc[i, ]),
    pvalue  = tt$p.value,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
de_prot$padj <- p.adjust(de_prot$pvalue, method = "BH")
sig_prot <- de_prot$Protein[which(de_prot$padj < 0.01 & abs(de_prot$log2FC) > 1.0)]

# Step 3: Functional macromolecular complexes
prot_modules <- list(
  "Cornified Envelope"          = c("FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3D", "SPRR2A"),
  "Desmosome Assembly"         = c("DSC1", "DSG1", "DSP", "PKP1"),
  "Serine Peptidase Inhibitors" = c("SPINK5", "SERPINB3", "SERPINB4"),
  "Antimicrobial Peptides"      = c("S100A7", "S100A8", "S100A9", "DEFB4A"),
  "Mitochondrial OxPhos"        = c("ATP5F1A", "NDUFS1", "COX4I1", "SDHA")
)

prot_ora <- cli_calc_ora(sig_prot, prot_modules, background = proteins)
prot_ora$MeanLog2FC <- vapply(prot_ora$Pathway, function(mod) {
  mean(de_prot$log2FC[de_prot$Protein %in% prot_modules[[mod]]])
}, numeric(1))

# Step 4: Compare across clinical phenotypes (AD vs HC and Psoriasis vs HC)
pso_shift <- c(-1.9, -1.4, 3.8, 1.8, 0.1)
prot_multi <- data.frame(
  Module   = rep(prot_ora$Pathway, 2),
  Contrast = rep(c("AD vs HC", "Psoriasis vs HC"), each = nrow(prot_ora)),
  Log2FC   = c(prot_ora$MeanLog2FC, pso_shift),
  negLogQ  = c(-log10(prot_ora$padj), c(4.8, 3.5, 9.2, 5.2, 0.2)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Step 5: Render diverging bubble heatmap
clitheme("nature")

p_prot_mod <- cliplot(
  Module ~ Contrast,
  data       = prot_multi,
  by         = prot_multi$negLogQ,
  type       = type_bubble_diverging(
    palette      = "nature",
    midpoint     = 0,
    max_size     = 8.0,
    stroke_col   = "grey30",
    stroke_width = 0.4,
    size_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)),
    fill_name    = expression(log[2]~"FC (Protein)")
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = prot_multi$Log2FC),
  title      = "Mass Spectrometry Deep Proteomics Functional Module Enrichment",
  subtitle   = "Circle size encodes -log10 q; diverging fill encodes protein abundance log2(FC)"
)
p_prot_mod
```

Cornified envelope proteins decreased in AD lesional skin (mean $\log_2(\text{FC}) = -2.41$, $q = 1.96 \times 10^{-5}$), while antimicrobial defense proteins increased (mean $\log_2(\text{FC}) = 3.19$, $q = 9.03 \times 10^{-5}$).

### Cutaneous Microbiome Functional Metagenomics (MetaCyc Pathways): A to Z Pipeline

Shotgun metagenomics profiles metabolic pathway abundance across skin microenvironments. The pipeline:

1. Filters low-prevalence pathways (detected in $< 20\%$ of samples).
2. Stabilizes variance with $\log_2(\text{CPM} + 1)$ transformation.
3. Tests differential abundance between flare and remission with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests.
4. Corrects for multiple testing across pathways and anatomical microenvironments.

```{r multiomics-microbiome-metacyc-atoz, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.8}
# Step 1: Input MetaCyc functional pathway counts (CPM) across skin sites
set.seed(42)
metacyc_paths <- c(
  "Staphyloferrin Siderophore Biosynthesis",
  "Peptidoglycan Maturation",
  "Lipoteichoic Acid Biosynthesis",
  "SCFA (Butyrate) Production",
  "L-Arginine Degradation",
  "Bile Acid Hydrolysis"
)
sites <- c("Antecubital Fossa", "Volar Forearm", "Forehead")
n_subj <- 12

# Step 2 & 3: Differential testing (Flare vs Remission) per site
mb_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sites, function(st) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(metacyc_paths, function(pwy) {
    flare_mean <- if (grepl("Staphyloferrin|Peptidoglycan|Lipoteichoic", pwy)) 5.2 else 2.1
    remis_mean <- if (grepl("Staphyloferrin|Peptidoglycan|Lipoteichoic", pwy)) 2.3 else 4.5
    
    flare_cpm <- pmax(0, rnorm(n_subj, mean = flare_mean, sd = 0.7))
    remis_cpm <- pmax(0, rnorm(n_subj, mean = remis_mean, sd = 0.7))
    
    wt <- wilcox.test(flare_cpm, remis_cpm)
    log2fc <- mean(flare_cpm) - mean(remis_cpm)
    prev <- mean(c(flare_cpm, remis_cpm) > 0.5) * 100
    
    data.frame(
      Pathway    = pwy,
      Site       = st,
      Log2FC     = log2fc,
      Prevalence = prev,
      pvalue     = wt$p.value,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))

# Step 4: Adjust p-values across all tests
mb_results$padj    <- p.adjust(mb_results$pvalue, method = "BH")
mb_results$negLogQ <- -log10(mb_results$padj)

# Step 5: Render diverging bubble heatmap across anatomical microenvironments
clitheme("nature")

p_mb_metacyc <- cliplot(
  Pathway ~ Site,
  data       = mb_results,
  by         = mb_results$negLogQ,
  type       = type_bubble_diverging(
    palette      = "rdbu",
    midpoint     = 0,
    max_size     = 8.0,
    stroke_col   = "grey35",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)),
    fill_name    = expression(log[2]~"FC (Flare / Remission)")
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = mb_results$Log2FC),
  title      = "Cutaneous Microbiome Functional Metagenomics (MetaCyc Pathways)",
  subtitle   = "Circle size encodes -log10 q; fill encodes flare vs remission log2(FC)"
)
p_mb_metacyc
```

Staphyloferrin siderophore biosynthesis had elevated abundance in flare lesions across all three cutaneous sites (antecubital fossa $\log_2(\text{FC}) = 3.79$, $q = 9.51 \times 10^{-7}$), whereas short-chain fatty acid production decreased ($\log_2(\text{FC}) = -2.46$, $q = 9.51 \times 10^{-7}$).


## Bubble Heatmap Archetypes: `type = "bubble_heatmap"`

Bubble heatmaps display two continuous variables across features (rows) and conditions (columns). Point size encodes magnitude, count, or significance; fill colour encodes directional effect size ($\log_2\text{FC}$, NES) or continuous significance ($-\log_{10}P$).

`cliomicplot` provides five bubble forms:
1. **Diamond Bubble Matrix**: classic diamond glyphs with alternating row bands.
2. **Circular Dot Bubble Matrix with Divergent Palette**: circular dots centered on zero to show positive and negative regulation.
3. **Significance-Glyph Annotated Matrix**: bubbles with significance asterisks (`*`, `**`, `***`) based on adjusted $P$-values.
4. **Square / Tile-Scaled Matrix**: proportional square glyphs in a tile grid.
5. **Directional Triangle Bubble Matrix**: oriented triangles indicating directional modulation across experimental cohorts.

### Form 1: Classic Diamond Bubble Matrix

Diamond bubble matrices display effect magnitude as diamond area and statistical significance as fill colour. Values exceeding `label_threshold` are labelled directly inside the glyphs.

```{r bubble-diamond-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.2}
set.seed(42)
proteins <- c("APOE", "MAPT", "APP", "SNCA", "GFAP", "NEFL", "VIM", "SYN1", "GAP43", "UCHL1")
contrasts <- c("AD vs Control", "PD vs Control", "AD vs PD", "Severe vs Mild")

bh_df <- expand.grid(Protein = proteins, Comparison = contrasts, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
bh_df$absFC <- runif(nrow(bh_df), 0.2, 3.5)
bh_df$negLogP <- runif(nrow(bh_df), 1.0, 15.0)

clitheme("cell")

p_diamond <- cliplot(
  Protein ~ Comparison,
  data       = bh_df,
  by         = bh_df$absFC,
  type       = type_bubble_diamond(
    max_size        = 8.0,
    size_name       = "|log2FC|",
    fill_name       = expression(-log[10]~P),
    fill_low        = "#4575B4",
    fill_mid        = "#FFFFBF",
    fill_high       = "#D73027"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = bh_df$negLogP),
  title      = "Diamond Bubble Matrix: Neurodegenerative Biomarkers",
  subtitle   = "Point size reflects |log2FC|; colour gradient reflects -log10 P"
)
p_diamond
```

### Form 2: Circular Dot Bubble Matrix with Divergent Palette

For bidirectional metrics such as Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) or signed $\log_2\text{FC}$, `type_bubble_diverging()` applies a diverging colour gradient centered at 0 (e.g. `palette = "nature"`: navy to white to red). Bubble radius represents $-\log_{10}q$.

```{r bubble-circle-diverging-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.2}
set.seed(101)
pathways_circ <- c(
  "IL-4 / IL-13 Signaling", "Th2 Differentiation", "JAK-STAT Cascade",
  "NF-kB Activation", "Epidermal Barrier", "Keratinization",
  "Lipid Metabolism", "Interferon Gamma Response"
)
stages <- c("Acute Lesional", "Chronic Lesional", "Non-Lesional", "Dupilumab W16")

da_df <- expand.grid(Pathway = pathways_circ, Stage = stages, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
da_df$NES <- c(
  2.4, 2.8, 0.4, -1.8,
  2.1, 2.5, 0.2, -1.5,
  1.8, 2.2, 0.5, -1.2,
  1.9, 1.7, 0.3, -0.9,
  -2.2, -2.6, -0.3, 1.9,
  -2.5, -3.1, -0.5, 2.2,
  -1.7, -2.1, -0.2, 1.4,
  0.6, 1.2, 0.1, -0.4
)
da_df$negLogQ <- runif(nrow(da_df), 1.5, 12.0)

clitheme("nature")

p_circ <- cliplot(
  Pathway ~ Stage,
  data       = da_df,
  by         = da_df$negLogQ,
  type       = type_bubble_diverging(
    palette      = "nature",
    midpoint     = 0,
    max_size     = 7.5,
    stroke_col   = "grey30",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)),
    fill_name    = "NES"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = da_df$NES),
  title      = "Inflammatory Pathway Modulation Across Disease Stages",
  subtitle   = "Circle size encodes -log10 q; diverging fill encodes Normalized Enrichment Score"
)
p_circ
```

### Form 3: Significance-Glyph Overlaid Matrix

When statistical significance requires explicit discrete thresholds ($* p < 0.05$, $** p < 0.01$, $*** p < 0.001$), `label_metric = "signif"` prints asterisks directly onto the bubbles.

```{r bubble-signif-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.2}
set.seed(202)
cytokines <- c("IL4", "IL13", "IL22", "IL31", "CCL17", "CCL18", "CCL26", "CXCL10", "IFNG", "IL1B")
timepoints <- c("Baseline", "Week 4", "Week 16", "Week 52")

cyt_df <- expand.grid(Cytokine = cytokines, Timepoint = timepoints, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cyt_df$log2FC <- runif(nrow(cyt_df), 0.2, 4.0)
cyt_df$negLogP <- runif(nrow(cyt_df), 0.5, 8.0)

clitheme("science")

p_signif <- cliplot(
  Cytokine ~ Timepoint,
  data       = cyt_df,
  by         = cyt_df$log2FC,
  type       = type_bubble_heatmap(
    shape          = "circle",
    palette        = "viridis",
    label_metric   = "signif",
    signif_cutoffs = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
    label_size     = 3.2,
    label_col      = "white",
    stroke_col     = "grey35",
    stroke_width   = 0.4,
    size_name      = expression(log[2]~"FC"),
    fill_name      = expression(-log[10]~P)
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = cyt_df$negLogP),
  title      = "Cutaneous Biomarker Response Kinetics",
  subtitle   = "Asterisks denote significance tiers (* p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001)"
)
p_signif
```

### Form 4: Square / Tile-Scaled Matrix

Proportional squares in a tile grid display cell density, taxon abundance, or cross-cohort concordance.

```{r bubble-square-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.0}
set.seed(303)
taxa <- c("S. aureus", "S. epidermidis", "C. acnes", "M. restricta", "P. melaninogenica", "C. striatum")
sites <- c("Volar Forearm", "Antecubital Fossa", "Forehead", "Cheek", "Retroauricular")

taxa_df <- expand.grid(Taxon = taxa, Site = sites, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
taxa_df$Abundance <- runif(nrow(taxa_df), 1.0, 30.0)
taxa_df$Prevalence <- runif(nrow(taxa_df), 20.0, 95.0)

clitheme("nejm")

p_square <- cliplot(
  Taxon ~ Site,
  data       = taxa_df,
  by         = taxa_df$Abundance,
  type       = type_bubble_square(
    palette      = "mako",
    max_size     = 8.0,
    stroke_col   = "white",
    stroke_width = 0.5,
    size_name    = "Rel. Abund (%)",
    fill_name    = "Prevalence (%)"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = taxa_df$Prevalence),
  title      = "Microbial Colonization Density Across Skin Microenvironments",
  subtitle   = "Square area reflects relative abundance; fill intensity reflects cohort prevalence"
)
p_square
```

### Form 5: Directional Triangle Bubble Matrix

Directional triangles (`shape = "triangle_up"` or `"triangle_down"`) emphasize activation or repression across experimental screens.

```{r bubble-triangle-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.0}
set.seed(404)
genes <- c("STAT3", "STAT6", "GATA3", "TBX21", "RORC", "FOXP3", "NFKB1", "RELA")
treatments <- c("Vehicle", "IL-4 Stim", "JAKi (Baricitinib)", "Biologic (Dupilumab)")

tri_df <- expand.grid(Gene = genes, Treatment = treatments, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
tri_df$Score <- runif(nrow(tri_df), 0.5, 5.0)
tri_df$Activity <- runif(nrow(tri_df), 1.0, 10.0)

clitheme("nature")

p_tri <- cliplot(
  Gene ~ Treatment,
  data       = tri_df,
  by         = tri_df$Score,
  type       = type_bubble_heatmap(
    shape        = "triangle_up",
    palette      = "rocket",
    grid_style   = "banded",
    max_size     = 8.0,
    stroke_col   = "white",
    stroke_width = 0.6,
    size_name    = "TF Score",
    fill_name    = "Activity Index"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = tri_df$Activity),
  title      = "Transcription Factor Activity Profile",
  subtitle   = "Triangle area encodes binding score; fill denotes computed activity index"
)
p_tri
```

## Rank-Abundance Dynamic Range Curves: `type = "rankabundance"`

In quantitative proteomics, rank-abundance curves visualize the dynamic range of protein detection across orders of magnitude:

```{r rank-abundance-demo, fig.width=8.0, fig.height=5.0}
set.seed(42)
n_prot <- 800
intensities <- sort(10^rnorm(n_prot, mean = 6.5, sd = 1.1), decreasing = TRUE)
ranks <- seq_len(n_prot)

rank_df <- data.frame(
  Rank      = ranks,
  Intensity = intensities,
  Protein   = paste0("Prot_", ranks)
)

clitheme("science")

p_rank <- cliplot(
  Intensity ~ Rank,
  data = rank_df,
  type = type_rankabundance(
    log_scale     = "10",
    point_color   = "#4DBBD5",
    marginal_type = "density",
    label_genes   = c("Prot_1", "Prot_10", "Prot_50", "Prot_200"),
    label_color   = "#E64B35",
    label_size    = 3.0
  ),
  title    = "Dynamic Range of Proteome Detection",
  subtitle = "Protein abundance spanning ~5 orders of magnitude with marginal density",
  xlab     = "Abundance Rank",
  ylab     = "LFQ Intensity"
)
p_rank
```
